items.title: How a Bruise Actually Forms and Changes Color
items.content_text: A bruise is blood trapped under unbroken skin, and its shifting colours track the chemical breakdown of haemoglobin as your body recycles the iron in it.

items.title: How a Candle Flame Actually Sustains Itself
items.content_text: A candle burns vapour, not solid wax. Its own flame melts, wicks and vaporises fuel in a self-regulating loop that stays stable for hours without any control.

items.title: How a Catalytic Converter Actually Cleans Exhaust
items.content_text: A catalytic converter uses a thin coating of precious metals to rearrange toxic exhaust gases into harmless ones, without being consumed in the process.

items.title: How a Microwave Oven Actually Heats Food
items.content_text: A microwave heats food by making water molecules flip billions of times a second, generating friction heat from the outside inward, not from the inside out.

items.title: How a Pin Tumbler Lock Actually Works
items.content_text: A pin tumbler lock turns only when every stack of spring-loaded pins is lifted to exactly the right height, aligning a hidden gap called the shear line.

items.title: How a Seatbelt Actually Locks in a Crash
items.content_text: A seatbelt stays loose until a steel ball or spinning weight senses sudden deceleration, then locks the reel instantly and manages how your body slows down.

items.title: How a Sunburn Actually Damages Skin Cells
items.content_text: Sunburn is not heat damage. Ultraviolet light breaks DNA directly, and the redness is your immune system clearing cells too damaged to repair safely.

items.title: How a Violin Actually Turns a String Into Sound
items.content_text: A vibrating violin string moves almost no air. The instrument's real job is converting that tiny motion into sound through a carefully tuned wooden box.

items.title: How Artificial Sweeteners Actually Trick Your Taste Buds
items.content_text: Sweeteners fit the tongue's sweet receptor far more tightly than sugar does, triggering an intense signal while passing through the body unused.

items.title: How Auctions Actually Set a Price
items.content_text: An auction does not discover what something is worth. It discovers what the most optimistic bidder will pay, which is a meaningfully different question.

items.title: How Composting Actually Turns Food Scraps Into Soil
items.content_text: Composting is controlled microbial digestion: bacteria and fungi break scraps down, generate their own heat, and leave behind stable humus that feeds soil.

items.title: How Creatine Actually Works in Muscle
items.content_text: Creatine is not a hormone or a stimulant. It recharges your muscles' fastest energy currency, letting you produce slightly more work before fatigue sets in.

items.title: How Fire Sprinklers Actually Decide to Activate
items.content_text: Fire sprinklers are not triggered by smoke and do not all go off together. Each head opens individually when heat bursts a small glass bulb above it.

items.title: How Hair Dye Actually Changes Hair Color
items.content_text: Permanent dye does not coat hair. It swells the shaft open, destroys your natural pigment, and builds new colour molecules trapped inside the fibre.

items.title: How Insurance Premiums Are Actually Calculated
items.content_text: An insurance premium is not a guess. It is your predicted average claim cost plus loading for expenses, uncertainty and profit, priced by statistical modelling.

items.title: How License Plate Recognition Actually Reads a Plate
items.content_text: Automatic plate recognition uses infrared light, reflective plate coatings and character recognition to read a number plate in milliseconds, day or night.

items.title: How Scars Actually Form and Why Some Fade
items.content_text: A scar forms because the body repairs deep wounds with fast, disorganised collagen instead of rebuilding the original skin structure it cannot replace.

items.title: How Superglue Actually Bonds in Seconds
items.content_text: Superglue does not dry. Trace moisture on every surface triggers a chain reaction that links its molecules into a solid plastic mesh within seconds.

items.title: How Tattoo Ink Actually Stays in Your Skin Permanently
items.content_text: Tattoo ink is permanent because immune cells swallow the pigment and stay put, trapping it in the dermis long after the wound itself has healed.

items.title: How Touchscreens Actually Know Where Your Finger Is
items.content_text: A modern touchscreen senses your finger by measuring tiny changes in an invisible electric field, not by detecting pressure or warmth from your hand.
